assessments.reasoning: The Index’s SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 includes terms governing relevant data. Its admission table at bytes [533,942) classifies an identifiable grant with a controlling text and edition as a license. Canada’s grant of rights in Information meets that criterion.

Both captures come from open.canada.ca/en/open-government-licence-canada. They cover bytes [0,16384) and [16384,23088) and report the claim’s full revision digest. The page identifies the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat as creator and English as its language. The first part supplies the Canadian title, conditional grant and exemptions. The second supplies the Crown definition and explicit v2.0 declaration.

The Index decision at afb962e68831a16accb80c70159b1e2f1fbb4dbc, bytes [4180,4397), names permanent ID a829049f5ace446d98ad7f7a7c57493a, Open Government Licence – Canada v2.0, ogl-canada-2-0, sha256:e62c3211e4bdc94fa4b6ca6bf541749c18b468c994ccae55e32603fafe7204cd, license, active. The opaque ID and revision match the claim. The SPDX identifier in that row does not establish textual equivalence across representations.

challenge.method: Checked the Canadian English route, creator metadata, grant, Definitions and Versioning sections against the French alternate link and the Index’s separate UK v2.0 row. Tested whether the grant covered all government information.
challenge.results: The English body explicitly names Canada and version 2.0. The French link identifies another representation, and UK v2.0 has a different entity and digest. The grant covers information offered under the licence and excludes, among other things, personal information and unauthorized third-party rights. The shared version number and an active registry value establish no broader coverage.

limitations: The English witness defines the Information Provider as “His Majesty the King in right of Canada.” The candidate records different monarch wording in the pinned SPDX text. That text was outside the supplied originals, so only the publisher side of the reported discrepancy was independently verified. The French representation is also outside scope.

The terms in force when the information was accessed govern its use. Attribution requirements and exemptions limit the grant. Application to a particular dataset, redistribution of license text, installation eligibility, SPDX status and consumer release authorization require separate evidence.
reasoning: The Government of Canada’s English publication expressly identifies version 2.0 and grants rights to use Information offered under its terms. That grant meets the Index’s license criterion for relevant data. The Index assigns active to the exact Canadian English witness.
